summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old woman with alcoholic cirrhosis, hepatic encephalopathy, and a history of chronic abdominal pain was admitted for acute-on-chronic lower abdominal pain radiating to the back and legs. She presented with confusion and visual hallucinations, attributed to stopping lactulose, rifaximin, and risperidone. Initial labs showed leukocytosis, but cultures were negative. CT and ultrasound revealed possible gastritis, a fibroid uterus, and a mildly dilated bile duct without obstruction. She developed melena and hematochezia during admission; upper endoscopy and colonoscopy showed no active bleeding source, but diverticulosis was noted. She received one unit of PRBCs and underwent capsule endoscopy, which showed no active bleed. Her mental status improved with medication re-initiation. Antibiotics were continued empirically for abdominal pain linked to prior UTIs. She was discharged home with optimized liver and psychiatric medications and instructions to follow up on capsule endoscopy results and possible MRI for persistent hallucinations and visual changes.
